Analyze the following legacy OSGi module extract and produce a comprehensive modernization blueprint.
USER PREFERENCE: The user chose NOT to generate backend Objects. Assume the Liferay Objects already exist or are migrated separately. DO NOT generate any Batch Client Extension. Focus strictly on generating the Frontend Custom Element Client Extension (calling /o/c/[slug]).

Determine:
1. Liferay Object definitions (ignoring audit fields like companyId, userId, createDate), ONLY if backend objects are requested.
2. Required Batch Client Extension structure, ONLY if backend objects are requested.
3. Frontend UI components (React JavaScript Custom Elements or Page Fragments), if portlets exist.
4. Model Listeners / Service Wrappers / custom LocalServiceImpl logic mapping (Native Object Actions vs a Spring Boot objectAction client extension),
   naming for each action: the object, the trigger, the executor, and the legacy class and method it replaces.
5. API CONTRACT (ALWAYS include it, even if backend objects are not generated): a section titled '## API CONTRACT' listing,
   for each Liferay Object: its name (PascalCase, e.g. DevconRegistration), its externalReferenceCode, and its REST endpoint
   '/o/c/' + the lowercase plural of the name with only letters and digits (e.g. '/o/c/devconregistrations');
   for each Picklist: its externalReferenceCode and its entries URL
   '/o/headless-admin-list-type/v1.0/list-type-definitions/by-external-reference-code/[ERC]/list-type-entries'.
   for each Object Action: its name, externalReferenceCode, trigger and executor; for each Notification Template: its externalReferenceCode;
   for each microservice: its client extension id and port.
   The backend and frontend coders work in parallel and never see each other's files: this contract is the ONLY way they agree on names, codes and URLs.

FORMAT: do NOT use Markdown tables anywhere in the blueprint; use headings and bullet lists (e.g. '- `title` (String, Text, required)'). Never draw lines of dashes.
Describe the design in prose and tables: NEVER write file contents (JSON, YAML, Java, JavaScript) in the blueprint; the coders write the files from the playbook templates.
Legacy columns with a reserved name (status, id, companyId, groupId, userId, userName, createDate, modifiedDate, uuid, externalReferenceCode) get a new field name prefixed with the entity (e.g. 'status' -> 'bookStatus'); list the rename in the API CONTRACT.
MICROSERVICE: plan at most ONE Spring Boot objectAction client extension per module ('[module-slug]-object-action', port 58081), with one Object Action per trigger;
logic of the same trigger runs in order inside it (e.g. compute the late fee, then send it to the inventory). Its OAuth scopes include 'c_[objectname].everything' (lowercase) when it updates entries.
'update-object-entry' only sets fixed values: computed values (dates such as 'today + 14 days', arithmetic, conditions on the previous value) go to the microservice.

THEME INVENTORY (the migrator writes the theme client extension 'acme-theme' itself, without AI: theme CSS from the theme's SCSS, its Style Book tokens, images and JavaScript. Do NOT generate it;
plan and generate only the header/footer fragments and master page that replace its FreeMarker templates and settings):
- Theme Acme Theme (acme)
- 11 SCSS sources, 6 of the theme's own: css/_clay_variables.scss, css/_custom.scss, css/acme/_header.scss, css/acme/_index.scss, css/acme/_sticky.scss, css/acme/_variables.scss
- 1 Style Book tokens in WEB-INF/frontend-token-definition.json
- 2 images and fonts of the theme, custom favicon (+ 0 base theme images, copied only if its SCSS uses them)
- JavaScript with code: js/sticky.js
- Templates: templates/navigation.ftl, templates/portal_normal.ftl
- Configurable settings: show-header-search, enable-sticky-header
- Not migrated: images/clay/icons.svg: the Clay icon set of the base theme (registering it as a spritemap would replace the current icons)
- Not migrated: js/main.js: the empty main.js of the theme generator

--- File: theme:liferay-look-and-feel.xml ---
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<look-and-feel>
	<compatibility><version>7.4.0+</version></compatibility>
	<theme id="acme" name="Acme Theme">
		<template-extension>ftl</template-extension>
		<settings>
			<setting configurable="false" key="color-palette" value="primary,secondary"/>
			<setting configurable="true" key="show-header-search" type="checkbox" value="true"/>
			<setting configurable="true" key="enable-sticky-header" type="checkbox" value="false"/>
		</settings>
	</theme>
</look-and-feel>


--- File: theme:navigation.ftl ---
<nav>${nav_items}</nav>


--- File: theme:portal_normal.ftl ---
<!DOCTYPE html>

<#include init />

<html class="${root_css_class}" dir="<@liferay.language key="lang.dir" />" lang="${w3c_language_id}">
<head>
	<title>${the_title} - ${company_name}</title>
	<@liferay_util["include"] page=top_head_include />
</head>
<body class="${css_class}">
<@liferay.control_menu />
<div id="wrapper">
	<header class="acme-header" id="banner">
		<a class="logo" href="${site_default_url}"><img alt="${logo_description}" src="${site_logo}" /></a>
		<span class="site-name">${site_name}</span>
		<#if getterUtil.getBoolean(themeDisplay.getThemeSetting("show-header-search"))>
			<div class="acme-search"><@liferay.search_bar /></div>
		</#if>
		<#include "${full_templates_path}/navigation.ftl" />
	</header>
	<section id="content">
		<@liferay_util["include"] page=content_include />
	</section>
	<footer class="acme-footer" id="footer">
		<p><@liferay.language key="powered-by" /> Acme</p>
	</footer>
</div>
<@liferay_util["include"] page=body_bottom_include />
</body>
</html>
